why: Cold spec-judge round 1 returned oracle FAIL and builder FAIL. Oracle: the spec-producer node -- the file this CR revises and the one that defines the restored bar -- still carried its own Use Cases as a bare trigger/inputs/outcome table, so the CR failed to apply its own bar to the one behavioral node it revised. Swept the rule (a CR restoring a bar applies it to every node it revises): 5 revised nodes, 4 are spec-type reference and carry Subject rather than Use Cases, so the judge's single instance was the complete set. Builder: the Architect duty added here (the CFG reaches every stated extension) had no producer-side mirror, violating this repo's own mirrored-duty rule; swept the other two new bar duties and both were already mirrored, so again a single instance. Writing the node's own extensions then surfaced two further defects the bar caught on its author: a Clearance stop stated as an extension when it is the conductor's decision across a co-owned seam, and a forbidden combination (USER_INPUT with BACKFILL) that is a precedence rule the procedure never refuses -- naming it would have asserted a guard nothing tests, the exact defect this CR names. Both struck. Three stated extensions had no scenario and gained one.

Cold impl-judge round 1: all 16 frozen scenarios PASS and no scenario inert under a 7-mutant sentence-level sweep, but BLOCKER on an orthogonal structural read. The producer procedure re-listed the five recurring extension kinds as a flat imperative while the format bar, its node, the website page and this CR's own changeset all carry the criterion plus the not-a-closed-set hedge -- and it did so in the very step whose preamble warns that a hardcoded list drifts from the bar. Self-undermining, and invisible to all 16 scenarios since none tests a divergence outside the five named kinds. Swept every re-list site in the diff: five total, three already hedged, exactly the two operational sites the judge named were bare. Both now carry the criterion and the hedge and defer to the bar that owns it. Also closed the judge's observation that the reachable-graph scenario was instructed only by inference -- an explicit amend-neither-side sentence replaces the inference -- and aligned the extensions:none marker to its literal form.

Cold impl-judge round 2 returned IMPLEMENTATION_PASS true with no blocker, and corrected the arithmetic in my own round-1 remediation record. I reported the re-list sweep as five sites, three already hedged; the real count is six sites, four hedged, because the changeset carries the list too and my grep pattern missed it. The substantive work was right -- both bare operational sites were found and fixed, and the judge's independent sweep found no sixth bare site -- but the count as written is false and both the commit message and the prior log line carry it. Recording the correct figure here rather than leaving a provenance record a later audit would have to catch. Also closed the judge's one loose thread: the website page's at-a-glance table row listed four of the five kinds with no hedge, so it now states the criterion instead of a partial list.

Owner folded two changes into an already-gate-passed CR and granted Clearance for the frozen-suite rewrite. First: the CR had created a rival source for the scenario set -- the standing rule derives scenarios from the CFG edges 1:1 on (path class, edge), and the CR added a per-extension rule at a different granularity, which is the knowledge duplication the structural bar forbids and risks the retrofit shape that has diverged here before. Corrected to one direction: the actor-centric extension search completes the CFG, and the CFG remains the sole source scenarios derive from. Second: the first pass improved use-case quality but left enumeration anchored on the surface in all three modes, and neither the scope nor the structural-fit bar carried any discovery obligation at all. Enumeration is now actor-first and checkable both ways, and the scope bar grades it. Swept for stale restatements of the replaced rule and found one the first pass missed: the coverage bar's own key-point read-check still carried the per-extension wording after its bar bullet had been rewritten.

Cold spec-judge round 3: architect FAIL and builder FAIL. Architect -- my sweep for stale restatements of the retracted rival-source rule reported one instance and missed three, all written by the original restore commit. One of the three was invisible to my sweep because the phrase straddles a line break, which a line-oriented search cannot see; re-running the sweep with whitespace normalized before matching reproduced the judge's three sites exactly. This is the second time in this CR that a stale restatement survived a sweep I reported as complete, and both times the residue sat in a summary block rather than a bar body. Builder -- the flagship actor-enumeration scenario failed its own miss test: its Given stipulated no actor-to-entry-point mismatch, so a producer that walks the interface, invents an actor per entry point and prints them above the table satisfied both Thens by construction. The judge demonstrated it against this CR's own self-application, where three use cases map onto three entry points with no mismatch. Its first Then was also an authoring-order assertion, unobservable in the artifact. Replaced with a Given the written interface cannot supply -- a party no entry point signature reveals -- plus a separate closure companion. Not a new narrowing: the gate was failing that scenario, so it was not agreed contract.

Cold spec-judge round 4 declared a REGRESSION, which stops the loop for a re-plan rather than another round. The finding names the exact paragraph the round-3 remediation commit edited: the node cites the spec-corpus spec-format README as owning the actor-first ordering, and that file does not carry it -- the ordering was added to the shipped skill only. Round 3 touched BOTH files and fixed neither, so the remediation missed its own dependency. Not treating this as one more site to patch. Rounds 2, 3 and 4 each found a different document where a new or retracted rule failed to propagate, after I reported each sweep as complete: first a key-point read-check, then three files one of which straddled a line break, now a spec-corpus node plus an untouched cross-linked website page carrying the pre-CR definition. Three misses across three sweeps is not bad luck, it is the corpus having three parallel layers -- shipped skill, spec-corpus node, public docs -- with nothing keeping them in sync and me sweeping ad hoc each round. Also outstanding and not a regression: the two CFG-routing scenarios carry a second Then asserting the scenario was DRAWN FROM the graph rather than merely matching it, which no finished artifact can reveal -- the same unobservable-authoring-order class the round-3 remediation existed to remove, recurring inside the replacement group it built.

Re-plan after the round-4 regression, not another patch round. Root cause named by the owner: a skill folder's members are one unit, and a change to any member should pull the whole folder into review -- nothing says so, so the members drift. Measured it rather than swept it again: of the six skill folders this CR touches, FIVE had an unmoved README.md. That is the regression's shape, systematically. Fixed the cited dependency (the spec-corpus spec-format node now carries the actor-first ordering the shipped skill had, which is what the stale citation claimed), reconciled the oracle and spec-producer skill READMEs, and found a second defect on the way -- the spec-producer README still cited sdd:spec-governance, a skill name retired some time ago. Also reconciled the website scenario page, which was untouched by this CR and still defined a use case as an entry point, so the two cross-linked pages described different things. Ran the closing sweep wrap-safe across all three layers with the plan, ledger, research and superseded-spec trees excluded; the only residue is two ADRs naming the pre-rename skill, which is correct for a dated decision record and one of which already carries its own stale-name update note.

The two CFG-routing scenarios each carried a second Then asserting the scenario was DRAWN FROM the graph rather than merely matching it. No finished artifact can reveal that -- a producer writing the scenario from prose and patching the graph afterward leaves an identical end state -- so it was the same unobservable-authoring-order shape the round-3 remediation existed to remove, recurring inside the replacement group it built. Both now assert that the SCENARIO MAP binds the scenario to the added path or guard edge, which is a fact the artifact carries and check-suite already lints under its 1:1 rule. The general move: stop trying to police authoring ORDER, which no product reveals, and instead assert the structural property the order was a proxy for.

Cold impl-judge round 3: all 22 frozen scenarios PASS on independent re-derivation, non-vacuity proven by a 9-mutant sentence-level sweep across all five duty groups (5 clean breaks; the 4 survivors each explained by real redundancy WITHIN the same file, an adjacent sentence or an earlier general rule, never inert text), absorption clean, extension criterion verbatim-consistent across all eight stating files, surface trace 9/9 against the real Inputs block. Blocked on one orthogonal structural finding: two of the five touched bar folders had a SKILL.md carrying the new duty and a README.md that did not. Resolved against the artifacts rather than by deferring to a judge: both READMEs carry an enumerated What-it-requires table meant to mirror the bar, so a missing row is drift and not silence -- which means the spec judge's earlier silence-is-not-drift ruling on the same two files was wrong. Third instance of the skill-folder-as-a-unit class in this CR. Checked all six touched folders rather than only the two named; the remaining mismatches are 7-line prose summaries carrying no duty enumeration and contradicting nothing, so one names the reordered seed-intent step accurately and the rest stand.

Cold impl-judge round 4: 22/22 frozen scenarios PASS, none inert under a 5-mutant sweep, absorption clean, and the round-3 remediation's own edits verified correct. Blocked on a fourth site of the same class -- the oracle bar's README duty table was missing BOTH duties this CR added, and the oracle spec-corpus node carried the surface-element duty but not the actor-enumeration one. My round-3 commit message had cited that same oracle README as the mirroring precedent for the fix; only its intro paragraph had been touched, never the table. Stopped hand-sweeping and compared mechanically instead: extracted every bar bullet from each governance SKILL and every duty row from its README across all five folders carrying both shapes. That flagged 8 candidate gaps; reading each rejected 3 as wording variants already present and confirmed the judge's 2 exactly, plus 2 more that predate this CR. Fixed the CR's own 2 and reconciled a third row the SKILL split had left stale. The pre-existing gaps are recorded, not fixed here.

note: Two governance bars carry a duty in their SKILL that their README duty table omits, both predating this change: the coverage bar at the spec gate is missing its non-author-evidence duty, and the same bar at the impl gate is missing its instrument-subject mutation-sweep-first duty. Found by a mechanical bar-to-table comparison rather than by reading. The comparison is about fifteen lines and belongs in the propagation work rather than in a manual sweep.
